Rashi on Sotah 23a:2:1.hebrew: וכל הנשואות [לכהנים] מנחותיהן נשרפות - ואפילו קרב הקומץ כהלכתו ולא נטמאו, נשרפין שירים בבית הדשן, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:2:1.english: And all [women] married [to priests], their meal-offerings are burned - Even if the handful (kometz) was offered properly and [the remainder] did not become impure, the remainders are burned in the place of the ashes (beit hadeshen), as the Gemara explains.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:2:2.english: A Kohenet - the daughter of a Kohen.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:2:3.hebrew: מנחתה נאכלת - דכל מנחת כהן כליל תהיה, לא תאכל כתיב (ויקרא ו׳:ט״ז). אבל כהנת הנשואה לישראל, נאכלת. וכן כהנת אלמנה וגרושה שהביאה מנחתה, נאכלת:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:2:3.english: Her meal-offering is eaten - For it is written, "Every meal-offering of a kohen shall be wholly burnt; it shall not be eaten" (Leviticus 6:16). But a kohenet [daughter of a kohen] who is married to an Israelite — [her offering] is eaten. And likewise, a kohenet who is a widow or a divorcée who brought her meal-offering — it is eaten.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:3:1.hebrew: כהנת מתחללת - מן התרומה ומן הכהונה, אם נבעלה לפסול:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:3:1.english: A priestess becomes disqualified - from terumah and from the priesthood, if she had relations with one who is disqualified [to her].

Rashi on Sotah 23a:3:2.hebrew: וכהן אין מתחלל - אם נשא גרושה זונה, וחללה. וטעם דכולה מתני' מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Sotah 23a:3:2.english: But a Kohen cannot be desecrated - If he married a divorcee [or] a zonah, and [thereby] desecrated her. And the reason for the whole Mishnah is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:4:1.hebrew: בקדשי קדשים - חטאת ואשם ומנחה, בכולם כתיב "כל זכר בכהנים [יאכלנו]":
Rashi on Sotah 23a:4:1.english: With regard to the most holy offerings - The sin-offering, the guilt-offering, and the meal-offering; with regard to all of them it is written, "Every male among the priests [may eat it]."

Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:1.hebrew: מה בין איש לאשה - בישראל נמי קמיירי:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:1.english: What is the difference between a man and a woman? - [The Mishnah] is speaking of an Israelite as well.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:2.hebrew: איש פורע ופורם - כשהוא מנוגע, פורע ראשו ופורם בגדיו:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:2.english: A man lets his hair grow loose and tears [his garments] - When he is afflicted with leprosy, he lets his head [of hair] grow loose and tears his garments.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:3.hebrew: האיש מדיר את בנו - קטן בנזיר, וחלה הנזירות עליו אפילו לכשיגדל:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:3.english: A man may place his son under a nazirite vow - [Though he is] a minor, [the father may bind him] as a nazirite, and the nazirite status takes effect upon him even when he grows up.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:4.hebrew: מגלח על נזירות אביו - אם נדר אביו בנזירות, והפריש קרבנותיו, ומת, והיה בנו נזיר — הבן מגלח ביום מלאת, ומביא קרבנות שהפריש אביו:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:5:4.english: He shaves for the nazirite vow of his father - If his father vowed to be a nazirite, set aside his offerings, and died, and his son was a nazirite, the son shaves on the day of completion [of the nazirite term] and brings the offerings that his father set aside.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:6:1.hebrew: מקדש את בתו - מקבל קידושי בתו קטנה שלא מדעתה:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:6:1.english: A man can betroth his daughter - He can accept the betrothal [money] of his minor daughter without her consent.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:6:2.hebrew: מוכר את בתו - לאמה, כשהיא קטנה:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:6:2.english: [A man] may sell his daughter - As a maidservant, when she is a minor.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:1.hebrew: מנחותיהן נשרפות - אחת מנחת סוטה, ואחת מנחת נדבה:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:1.english: Their meal-offerings are burned - Both the meal-offering of a sota and a voluntary meal-offering.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:2.hebrew: מפני שיש לו חלק בה - שהוא מקריבה משלו, וכתיב: כל מנחת כהן וגו':
Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:2.english: Because he has a share in it - For he offers it from his own [property], and it is written: "Every meal-offering of a priest [shall be wholly burnt; it shall not be eaten]" (Leviticus 6:16), etc.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:3.hebrew: ואינה עולה כליל שיש לה חלק בה - שלכפרתה היא באה, ואין מנחת זר ובת כהן קריבין כליל בלא קמיצה:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:3.english: And it is not offered up entirely [as a burnt offering], for she has a share in it - For it comes for her atonement; and the meal-offering of a non-priest and of a priest's daughter are not offered entirely [on the altar] without a kemitzah (a handful being taken).

Rashi on Sotah 23a:7:4.english: The remainder is offered by itself - After the handful has been offered.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:8:1.english: Read here: Anything from it, etc. - "For any leaven and any honey you shall not offer to the Lord" (Leviticus 2:11). [The verse] should have been written [without "from it"]. Why did it need to write "from it"? Rather, to expound it also on its own: "You shall not burn" anything from which [a portion] has already gone up as a fire-offering to the Lord. And included in this prohibition is the flesh of all offerings except the burnt-offering, and included in it are the remainders of meal-offerings. And here too, perhaps we should follow her portion, and the burning of the handful would be done properly, and these are fully remainders, and they are covered by "you shall not burn."

Rashi on Sotah 23a:8:2.hebrew: דמסיק להו לשם עצים - דנימא הכי: אם ראויים הן להקטיר, ולא היתה ראויה ליקמץ כדין מנחת כהן, הרי זו הקטרה לשמה, וקמיצה לא מעלה ולא מורדת. ואם ראויה היתה ליקמץ, ואלו שיריה — הרי הן כשאר עצי המערכה:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:8:2.english: For he burns them for the sake of wood - For let us say as follows: If they [the remainder and the handful] are fit to be burned, and [the offering] was not fit to have a handful taken from it, like the law of a priest's meal-offering, then this is a burning for its own sake, and taking the handful neither raises nor lowers [its status]. But if it was fit to have a handful taken from it, and these are its remainder, they are like the rest of the wood of the altar's arrangement.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:8:3.hebrew: כר"א - פלוגתייהו בזבחים: אברי חטאת שנתערבו באברי עולה, ר"א אומר יתנם למעלה, ורואה אני את בשר חטאת על המזבח כאילו הן עצים; וחכ"א תעובר צורתן ויצאו לבית השריפה, שאסור להקטיר אברי חטאת משום לאו דכל שממנו לאישים. ור"א סבר: בתריה דההוא קרא כתיב "קרבן ראשית תקריבו אותם לה'" — שאור ודבש; בכורים אתה מביא מן התמרים, ומנחת שתי הלחם שהוא ראשית מן השאור — "ואל המזבח לא יעלו לריח ניחוח", קאי נמי אממנו אשה לה', דאוקמיה בבל תקטירו. ואשמעינן דלא אסר הקטרתו אלא כשמתכוין לריח ניחוח:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:8:3.english: Like R. Eliezer - Their dispute is in Zevachim, [concerning] limbs of a sin-offering that were mixed up with limbs of a burnt-offering. R. Eliezer says: he places them all on top [of the altar], and I regard the flesh of the sin-offering on the altar as if it were wood. But the Sages say: let their form be disfigured, and they go out to the place of burning, since it is forbidden to offer up the limbs of a sin-offering because of the prohibition of "any part of it [may not be offered] as a fire-offering." And R. Eliezer holds: right after that verse it is written, "As an offering of first produce you shall bring them to the Lord" — [referring to] leaven and honey; [that is,] you bring first-fruits from dates, and the offering of the Two Loaves, which is the first [offering] from leaven — "but they shall not go up to the altar for a pleasing aroma." This too refers back to "any part of it as a fire-offering to the Lord," which was interpreted as [the prohibition of] "you shall not burn." And it teaches us that [the Torah] forbade burning it only when one intends it for a pleasing aroma.

Rashi on Sotah 23a:9:1.hebrew: כר"א בר"ש - במנחות בפ' אלו מנחות (מנחות דף עג:) גבי מנחת חוטא כהן, שמביא על שמיעת קול או על ביטוי שפתים או על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו בדלי דלות. ופליגי רבנן עליה דרבי שמעון ואמרי: והיתה לכהן כמנחה — מנחת חובתו של כהן כליל, כמנחת נדבתו, ואינה נקמצת. [ור"ש דריש ליה לקרא התם הכי: וכי נאמר והיתה לכהן כמנחתו? לא נאמר אלא] כמנחת חוטא של ישראל — מה של ישראל נקמצת, אף מנחת חוטא של כהן נקמצת. אי מה מנחת ישראל שיריה נאכלין, אף זו שיריה נאכלין? ת"ל והיתה לכהן כמנחה — לכהן כמנחה לענין עבודת כהן, שטעונה קמיצה, ולא לאישים כמנחה. הא כיצד? הקומץ קרב לעצמו, והשיריים קריבין לעצמם. ולית ליה כל שממנו לאישים כלל. ר"א בר"ש פליג עליה ואמר: קומץ קרב לעצמו, ושירים מתפזרין לאיבוד:
Rashi on Sotah 23a:9:1.english: Like R. Elazar b. R. Shimon - In Menachot, in the chapter "Eilu Menachot" (Menachot 73b), regarding the sin-offering meal-offering of a Kohen — which he brings for [having heard] a voice [of adjuration], or for a verbal utterance [of an oath], or for impurity of the Temple and its sanctified things, when [his means are reduced to] the lowest poverty. And the Rabbis disagree with R. Shimon there and say: "And it shall be for the Kohen, like the meal-offering" — the obligatory meal-offering of a Kohen is burned entirely, like his voluntary meal-offering, and it is not scooped [by the handful]. [And R. Shimon expounds the verse there as follows: Is it said, "And it shall be for the Kohen like his meal-offering"? It says only] "like the sin-offering meal-offering of an Israelite" — just as that of an Israelite is scooped, so too the sin-offering meal-offering of a Kohen is scooped. [One might think] that just as the remainder of an Israelite's meal-offering is eaten, so too the remainder of this one is eaten? Therefore the verse states, "And it shall be for the Kohen, like the meal-offering" — "for the Kohen, like the meal-offering" with regard to the Kohen's service, that it requires scooping; but not "like the meal-offering" with regard to the fires of the altar. How is this so? The handful is offered by itself, and the remainders are offered by themselves. And [R. Shimon] does not hold at all [the principle of] "anything of which a portion goes to the altar fires." R. Elazar b. R. Shimon disagrees with him and says: The handful is offered by itself, and the remainders are scattered and destroyed.

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:1:1.hebrew: האומרת טמאה אני - ירושלמי: האומרת "טמאה אני" — לא כחטאת שמתה בעליה היא? וחטאת שמתה בעליה — ילכו המעות לים המלח. דמיא לאשם תלוי? אם לאשם תלוי — אפי' משקדשה בכלי? א"ר: מתני' דמיא לאשם תלוי שנשחט, דתנינן תמן: אם משנשחט נודע לו — הדם ישפך והבשר יצא לבית השריפה:
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:1:1.english: One who says, "I am impure" - Yerushalmi: [Regarding] one who says, "I am impure" — is she not like a sin-offering whose owner has died? And [regarding] a sin-offering whose owner has died, the money goes to the Dead Sea. Is it comparable to a conditional guilt-offering (asham taluy)? If [it is comparable] to a conditional guilt-offering, [would that apply] even after she has sanctified it in a vessel? R. [...] said: Our Mishnah is comparable to a conditional guilt-offering that was [already] slaughtered, as we learned there: If it became known to him after it was slaughtered, the blood is to be poured out and the flesh goes out to the place of burning.

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:1:2.hebrew: ושבעלה בא עליה בדרך - תימה לר"י: אמאי נשרפת? כיון דבדרך בא עליה, היינו קודם שתקדוש, וכיון דאין המים בודקין אותה, כדאמר "ונקה האיש מעון" — בזמן שהאיש מנוקה מעון וכו' — תיגלי מילתא למפרע דכי קדוש בטעות קדוש, כדאמרינן גבי "ושבאו לה עדים שהיא טמאה": דהואיל ולא לבדוק עומדת, ולא ראויה למנחה, לא היתה ראויה לכלי, ואין כלי שרת מקדשין אלא בראוי להן. ונראה דדוקא לגבי שבאו לה עדים שייך למימר הכי, משום דמנחה לברר עון, וכשיש שם עדים הרי העון מבורר וא"צ בירור. אבל הכא שבא עליה בדרך, שצריך לברר, אע"ג דאין המים בודקין, כי קדוש מעיקרא שפיר קדוש, מאחר שלא נתברר העון, ולא הוי אלא כמו שנשאו ונתנו בה מוזרות בלבנה קודם לכן, דאין המים בודקין, ואפ"ה מנחה שפיר קדוש. והאי דלא חשיב במתני' מנחת ארוסה ושומרת יבם אלמנה לכ"ג — מפני שידוע פסול שלהן, שאינן נבדקות ואין מביאין אותם לשתות:
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:1:2.english: "And [if] her husband had relations with her on the way" - Rabbeinu Yitzchak (the Ri) was puzzled: Why is [her offering] burned? Since he had relations with her on the way, that was before she was sanctified [as a meal-offering]. And since the water does not test her, as it says, "and the man shall be clean of iniquity" — when the man is clean of iniquity, etc. — it should be revealed retroactively that when [the offering] was sanctified, it was sanctified in error, as we say regarding "and [if] witnesses came [and testified] that she is impure": Since she is not standing to be tested, she is not fit for the meal-offering, and so she was not fit for the vessel, and service vessels sanctify only what is fit for them. And it appears that this reasoning applies specifically to a case where witnesses came [and testified against her], because the meal-offering is meant to clarify the iniquity, and when there are witnesses there the iniquity is already clarified and needs no clarification. But here, where he had relations with her on the way, so that clarification is still needed, even though the water does not test her, [the offering] was sanctified properly from the outset, since the iniquity was not clarified. It is no different than if they had dealt with her (nasu venatnu bah) [with] muzarot in levanah beforehand, [a case] where the water does not test, and even so the meal-offering is validly sanctified. And as for the fact that the Mishnah does not list the meal-offering of a betrothed woman, a woman awaiting her yavam, or a widow [married] to a High Priest — [this is] because their disqualification is known, as they are not tested and are not brought to drink.

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:2:1.hebrew: כל הנשואות לכהנים מנחותיהן נשרפות - פרש"י: אחד מנחת סוטה ואחד מנחת נדבה. ותימה: מנחת נדבה מה חלק יש לו בה? והא אפילו רבי יהודה דאומר בפ' אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לה:): "אדם מביא על אשתו כל קרבנות שהיא חייבת" — דווקא שהיא חייבת, כדמפרש בספרי: כגון אם [הקיפה] נזירות בראשה וחיללה את השבת, דומיא דמנחת סוטה שהיא חובה, דיליף לה מ"והביא את קרבנה עליה" — כל קרבן שעליה. אבל מנחת נדבה מודה רבי יהודה שאינו מביא. וי"ל: משום הכי יש לו חלק, משום דקי"ל מה שקנתה אשה קנה בעלה, כדתנן בפ"ד דנזיר (דף כד.): "אם שלה היתה בהמה, החטאת תמות", וקא דייק בגמ': מנא לה? מה שקנתה אשה קנה בעלה. הלכך יש לו חלק בה, אפילו לרבנן דפליגי אדר' יהודה ואמרי דווקא קרבן שמכשירה לו מביא עליה, דמה שקנת' קנה בעלה. מיהו בירושלמי דפרק היה מביא משמע דבמנחת סוטה איירי, והכי איתא התם: "מנחתה — מלמד שהיא קדשה לשמה, כשם שהיא קדשה לשמה כך היא קדשה לשמו. ותני רבי חייא ופליג: ליקרב כליל — אינה יכולה, מפני שותפתה של אשה; לאכול — אינה יכולה, מפני שותפתו של איש; [אלא] הקומץ לעצמו והשירים קריבין לעצמן. ואת אומר מנחתה? אלא מה דאישתעי קרא אישתעי, מתני'". ותו התם: "והביא את קרבנה עליה — בעלה, מהו שיפריש עליה חוץ מדעתה? מכיון שיש לו שותפות במנחה, מפריש עליה חוץ מדעתה". וא"ת: מאחר שיש לו חלק בה, א"כ הויא לה מנחת שותפות, ואומר בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ה:): "הניח מנחה לשני בניו ומת — קריבה, ואין בה משום שותפות"; הא יש בה משום שותפות — אינה קריבה, משום דכתיב בה "נפש". והכי קתני בסיפרי בהדיא. וי"ל: כיון דעיקר כפרה משום דידה, "נפש" קרינן בה; דהא "הניח מנחתו לשני בניו" דמסיק התם (דף ו.) דקניא להו — אלמא משום דמכפרי קרינא ביה "נפש":
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:2:1.english: "All [women] married to priests — their meal-offerings are burned" - Rashi explains: Both the meal-offering of a sotah and a voluntary meal-offering. And this is astonishing: [regarding] a voluntary meal-offering, what share does he [the husband] have in it? For even Rabbi Yehudah, who says in the chapter "Ein Bein HaMudar" (Nedarim 35b): "A man may bring on behalf of his wife all the offerings that she is obligated to bring" — [that applies] specifically to what she is obligated [to bring], as is explained in the Sifrei: for example, if she took a nazirite vow upon her head and then desecrated the Shabbat; similar to the meal-offering of a sotah, which is an obligation, as he derives it from "and he shall bring her offering for her" — any offering that is incumbent upon her. But regarding a voluntary meal-offering, Rabbi Yehudah agrees that he does not bring it. And one can answer: He has a share in it for this reason — because we hold that what a woman acquires, her husband acquires, as we learned in the fourth chapter of Nazir (24a): "If the animal was hers, the sin-offering must die," and the Gemara there inquires: From where [do we know] this? [From the principle that] what a woman acquires, her husband acquires. Therefore he has a share in it, even according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehudah and say that he brings on her behalf only an offering that makes her fit for him, since what she acquires, her husband acquires. However, in the Yerushalmi, in the chapter "Haya Mevi," it implies that [the Mishnah] is speaking about the meal-offering of a sotah, and this is what it says there: "'Her meal-offering' — this teaches that it is consecrated for her sake; just as it is consecrated for her sake, so it is consecrated for his sake. And Rabbi Chiyya taught, and disagrees: It cannot be offered whole [on the altar], because of the woman's partner; it cannot be eaten [by the priests], because of the man's partner; rather, the handful [is offered] for itself and the remainder is offered for itself. And you say 'her meal-offering'? Rather, what Scripture says, it says; [so too] the Mishnah." And further there: "'And he shall bring her offering for her' — her husband: may he set it aside for her without her knowledge? Since he has a partnership in the meal-offering, he may set it aside for her without her knowledge." And if you ask: Since he has a share in it, then it should be a meal-offering of partnership, yet it says in the first chapter of Zevachim (5b): "If someone left a meal-offering to his two sons and died, it is offered, and it is not subject to [the problem of] partnership"; [which implies that] where there is [the problem of] partnership, it is not offered, because the word "soul" (nefesh) is written regarding it. And so the Sifrei explicitly teaches. One can answer: Since the main atonement is on her account, we call it a "soul"; for in the case of "he left his meal-offering to his two sons," which the Gemara there (6a) concludes that it was acquired for them — evidently, because they are atoned by it, we call it a "soul."

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:7:1.hebrew: הקומץ קרב בעצמו - וא"ת: אמאי לא שדינן לכולה מנחה בתר דידה, ויהו שיריה נאכלין? כדאמר בפ' אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לו:), ואיתא בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ו.) ובפ"ק דתמורה (דף ב:): מתכפר עושה תמורה, והכא היא מתכפרת במנחה זו. י"ל: התם מיקני למתכפר כולי זבח, ואין לו למקדיש חלק בו; אבל הכא יש לו לבעל חלק במנחה:
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:7:1.english: The handful is offered by itself - And if you ask: Why do we not cast the entire meal-offering after her [i.e., treat the whole offering as hers], so that its remainder would be eaten? As is stated in the chapter "Ein Bein HaMudar" (Nedarim 36b), and it is found in the first chapter of Zevachim (6a) and in the first chapter of Temurah (2b): The one who achieves atonement [through the offering] is the one who can make a substitute [for it]; and here, she achieves atonement through this meal-offering. One can answer: There, the entire sacrifice is acquired by the one achieving atonement, and the one who consecrated it has no share in it; but here, the husband has a share in the meal-offering.

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:8:1.hebrew: דמסיק להו לשום עצים - רש"י פי': דנימא הכי, אם ראוין הן להקטיר ולא היתה ראויה לקמוץ וכו'. ותימה: מאי תנאי שייך? הא ודאי כאילו מעורבין שיריים, והוי כאברי עולה ואברי חטאת שנתערבו, דפליגי בה ר"א ורבנן (זבחים עז.), דלא שייך בה תנאי, דליכא שום ספק; אלא ודאי מקצתן ראויה להקטיר ומקצתן לאכול. ולהקטיר, ואותן מה שבתוכן אין ראוי להקטיר — לשם עצים בכל מקום שהוא, ולא שייך שום תנאי. וכמדומה דרש"י נקט לי' אגב שטפיה דההיא דפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות ק.), דתנן: "כהנת שנתערב ולדה בולד שפחתה, נותנין עליהם חומרי ישראל וחומרי כהנים", ומפרש בגמרא דמנחתם נקמצת כמנחת ישראל, ואינה נאכלת כמנחת כהנים; וכולה סוגיא כי הכא. והתם ודאי שייך תנאי: כשהאחד מקריב מנחה, אינו יודע אם כהן הוא או ישראל, וצריך להתנות, כמו שפירש רש"י כאן. והא דתנן בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כג.): "נתערב קומצה בשיריה או בשירים של חבירתה, לא יקטיר" — אית לן למימר דסתמא כרבנן, דפליגי אדרבי אליעזר:
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:8:1.english: "That he adds them for the sake of wood" - Rashi explains that we should say as follows: if they are fit to be burned, but she was not fit for the removal of the handful (*kemitzah*), etc. But this is puzzling: what condition could apply here? Surely it is as if the remainders were mixed together, and it is like the limbs of a burnt offering and the limbs of a sin offering that became mixed, about which Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree (Zevachim 77a), where no condition applies, since there is no doubt at all; rather, it is certain that some of them are fit to be burned and some to be eaten. And as for burning, those among them that are not fit to be burned are burned for the sake of wood, wherever they are, and no condition applies at all. It seems that Rashi mentioned this out of the momentum of that passage in the chapter "Nosin Al HaAnusah" (Yevamot 100a), where we learned: "If a *kohen*'s daughter's child was mixed up with the child of her maidservant, we apply to them both the stringencies of an Israelite and the stringencies of *kohanim*," and the Gemara explains that their meal offering has a handful removed, like the meal offering of an Israelite, and is not eaten, like the meal offering of *kohanim*; and that whole passage is like ours here. There, a condition certainly applies: when one of them brings a meal offering, he does not know whether he is a *kohen* or an Israelite, and he must stipulate, as Rashi explained here. And as for what we learned in Chapter "HaKometz Rabbah" (Menachot 23a): "If its handful was mixed with its remainder, or with the remainder of another's meal offering, he may not burn it," we must say that this [Mishnah] is anonymous and follows the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer:

Tosafot on Sotah 23a:9:1.hebrew: הקומץ קרב לעצמו והשיריים לעצמן - בירושל' בעי אליביה דר"ש: אלין שיריים, משום מה הם באים? משום קומץ או משום שיריים? אי תימר משום קומץ — אינו נותנו בלילה, ואינו נותנו לאחר מיתה, ואינו מחשב להן; ואי תימר משום שיריים — נותנו בלילה, ונותנו לאחר מיתה, מהו שיחשב להן? ופשיט לה מדר"א בר"ש, דאמר דמתפזרין על גבי הדשן שלמטה, כדמפרש בפ' ואלו הן מנחות: הדא אמרו נותנו בלילה ונותנו לאחר מיתה, ומחשב להן. א"ר יוסי בר בון: אינו מחשב להו, שלא הוכשרו לא לאכילת אדם ולא לאכילת מזבח:
Tosafot on Sotah 23a:9:1.english: The *kometz* is offered on its own, and the remainders on their own - In the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] raises a question according to Rabbi Shimon: These remainders, why do they come — because of the *kometz* or because of the remainders themselves? If you say [they come] because of the *kometz*, then one may not place it at night, and may not place it after [the owner's] death, and one cannot form [invalidating] intention regarding them. And if you say [they come] because of the remainders, then one may place it at night, and may place it after [the owner's] death; but can one form intention regarding them? And it resolves this from Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, who said that they are scattered over the ashes below, as is explained in the chapter *Eilu Hen HaMenachot*: From this they said that one may place it at night, and may place it after death, and one can form intention regarding them. Rabbi Yose bar Bun said: One cannot form intention regarding them, because they were made fit neither for human consumption nor for consumption by the altar:
